problem.title: Tickets in the Drawer
problem.statement: A drawer contains r unused tickets and 18 used tickets, for 45 tickets altogether. Which value of r makes r + 18 = 45 true?
hints: Undo the added 18 on both sides.

solutionSteps.title: Preserve equality
solutionSteps.body: Subtract 18 from both sides: r + 18 - 18 = 45 - 18, so r = 27.

solutionSteps.title: Check
solutionSteps.body: 27 + 18 = 45, so the original total is correct.

validationMethods: independent substitution and option audit: only 27 + 18 equals 45
notes: The prompt supplies the equation so it isolates equality-preserving subtraction without additional translation load.

problem.title: Six Equal Packs
problem.statement: Six identical packs contain 42 markers altogether. If p is the number of markers in one pack, what value of p makes 6p = 42 true?
hints: Split both sides into six equal groups.
Multiply your proposed pack size by six to check.

solutionSteps.title: Check
solutionSteps.body: Six packs of seven markers contain 6(7) = 42 markers.

validationMethods: equal-group derivation: 42 markers divided among 6 packs gives 7 per pack
independent multiplication and option audit: only 6 × 7 equals 42

problem.title: Farm Stand Earnings
problem.statement: A farm stand begins the day with 11 dollars in change and earns 4 dollars for each basket sold. At one point the cash box holds 47 dollars. If b baskets have been sold, what is b?
hints: Undo the fixed 11 before dividing by four.

solutionSteps.title: Write and simplify
solutionSteps.body: The relationship is 4b + 11 = 47. Subtract 11 from both sides to get 4b = 36.

solutionSteps.title: Isolate and check
solutionSteps.body: Divide both sides by 4 to get b = 9. Then 4(9) + 11 = 47.

validationMethods: independent forward construction and option audit: starting at 11 and adding nine groups of 4 reaches 47; no other choice does

problem.title: The Same Unknown on Both Sides
problem.statement: Which value of x makes 3x + 9 = 2x + 17 true?
hints: Check that both original expressions have the same value.

solutionSteps.title: Preserve equality
solutionSteps.body: Subtract 2x from both sides to get x + 9 = 17.

solutionSteps.title: Finish and check
solutionSteps.body: Subtract 9 from both sides, giving x = 8. Both original sides then equal 33.

validationMethods: symbolic difference: subtracting 2x and 9 from both sides yields x = 8
independent exhaustive option substitution: left and right are equal only at choice C, where both equal 33

problem.title: Consecutive Sum
problem.statement: Two consecutive positive integers have sum 41. What is the larger integer?
hints: Represent the smaller integer by n and the next one by n + 1.

solutionSteps.title: Translate
solutionSteps.body: Let n be the smaller integer. Then n + (n + 1) = 41.

solutionSteps.title: Solve
solutionSteps.body: Combine like terms: 2n + 1 = 41. Subtract 1 from both sides and divide both sides by 2, giving n = 20.

validationMethods: algebraic derivation: n + (n + 1) = 41 gives n = 20 and larger integer 21
independent parity and adjacency check: the pair centered on 20.5 is 20 and 21; only choice C is the larger member and the sum is 41
